atoms.b: Light consists of a spectrum of colours. They appear white when observed ((++together separately)).
What are the colours in the spectrum of light?
The light spectrum consists of the colours red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. These colours can commonly be seen in ((++rainbows refractions)).
Why are some objects lighter or darker than others?
The more light an object reflects, the ((++lighter darker)) it appears. The less light it reflects, the ((lighter ++darker)) it appears.
Why do different objects appear in different colours?
Some objects only reflect parts of the light spectrum and absorb the rest. We see an object as the colour that it ((++reflects absorbs)).
Yes, this apple reflects ((++only no)) red light and ((++absorbs reflects)) the rest.
